title: Feels good to finally make progress
body:
Each year I make new year resolutions and find that by March I have forgotten them or moved on to the next pressing thing. Even using reminders in calendar to review progress quarterly didn't help much. That is why this year I went hunting for a way to change my habits. That's right habits; not just goals. I read a lot of reviews and tested several apps but Strides comes up top. 

The free app has so much stuff you don't even need to pay for the premium features. It is easy to use and has such easy ways of tracking progress. It uses gentle reminders and nudges when you are falling behind. Best part is that it tracks goals (the desired end result), milestones (markers along the way) and even habits (to see that the behavior sticks). Some goals are really tough to keep but with Strides I find swiping a completed target rather fulfilling. 

Try it out for yourself, you'll be pleasantly surprised.

title: Absolutely beautiful, but no API to automate tracking
body: The data visualizations are beautiful and it would be a lovely place to visualize data from a variety of habits and goals. Sadly, there is no API and no integration with any services like IFTTT or Zapier. As a result, you can only really track a few things before the friction of manual data entry is just too much to be sustainable. If you only want to track a few things and you’re fine with doing that manually, then I think this is probably a great app for you. If you want to seamlessly and automatically track many different things, it’s probably worth finding something else. I found the friction of manual data entry to be too high a price for the visualizations, and moved to something else. In the end, the beautiful visualizations weren’t of any use to me if the friction of the data entry was such that I wasn’t entering any data to visualize…

title: Comprehensive Tracking Tool!
body:
After trying some free and cheap tracking tools I decided to give Strides a try, despite of the price (free trial for 7 days).

First, I wanted an app to track everything, and sometimes how I did it (frequency, length, duration etc.)… so I needed it to do more than just a check-box.

Once I started using it, I fell in love. It is well designed with different types of tracking (habit, target, average & project) to fit different needs, and under each tracker there are many customizable options on how you want to track or be reminded/celebrated.
And it works very well with iWatch.

And the progression and result page are nicely presented and easy to read. It actually encourages me to get things checked more so I can see more green! 

I am planning to buy the life time subscription, I can see myself use it for a long time.

title: Great app, boring UI, only 3 Free Trackers.
body:
Gets the job done but I was sad to see they’ve joined their competitors in reducing their free trackers from 7 to 3.

Monthly subscription does not offer anywhere near enough to justify $6.99/ month. 

Aside from the lacklustre UI, and the high monthly price, this app actually does everything else right. Except that it’d also be nice to be able to click on the individual month in graph view for a particular tracker and have it take you to that month to see the months data. Only way to get to a month 2 years ago now is to swipe through the months all the way back. 

Shouldn’t ads be enough to cover a few extra trackers for free? How about a price per month that varies depending on the trackers and other features required? 

The one time fee is ridiculous. A triple A video game is much cheaper and costs so much more to develop and I have the right to play the game and receive updates for life as well but for 2/3 of the price of Strides!
Sorry but the difference in value proposition is astronomical! 

Had to go looking elsewhere...

title: Costs 79€ to unlock
body:
Really good app. Would definitely pay for it to unlock some premium function. But monthly payments? Come on. Or they want 79.99€ to unlock all features without an subscription. Back in the days, an app like this would have cost maybe 5 or 10€ and then you actually own the app. Now you have to rent it, or pay an insane 79.99€ to buy yourself free of subscription payments.
I used to pay for this app back in the days when they used their own servers to sync data. Now they use iCloud to sync (at no cost for the developers), no reason for a subscription payment anymore.  
Every single app wants an subscription for basic features nowadays, this is getting out of hands. 79.99€ I usual pay for complex Mac Software like video/photo editing software. But not for an simple iPhone habit tracker.

title: Good, great potential, expensive
body:
The app in its current state, while missing some key features, remains the best in its class.

I enjoy the ease of use, and how they managed to keep it configurable yet intuitive. It's nice to have 4 different tracker types to choose from, although it's a bit of a let down that the suggested trackers are only titles, and not pre-populated templates.

Looking forward to filters for active tracker hours and to exclude completed trackers.

The subscription model is expensive - too expensive for many but I guess they're expecting a high end customer for an almost high end app. They should really start the subscription at a more affordable price. Unsurpassed features are what would allow price increases in the future.

Their feature request & voting service lists some of those missing key features as planned for the current version but seem to have been pushed back to a later release. I hope they eventually get around to implementing them.

title: Thanks guys! Review 3.0

2024: I’m still here! Life has been hectic lately and I was inconsistent with my habits and daily routine but hence I’m planning to improve I am willing to become consistent with using Strides again. I was just wondering if it would be helpful for the creators to include some writing about the benefits of sticking to the goals, being consistent, that there isn’t such thing as a fail but room to improve? 

2021 update: I switched to newer phone but I still stuck with the strides app! My views haven’t changed. For a period of time I was too overwhelmed with everything around that I started to ignore the strides, but after few weeks I got back to using it again. It helped me get back on track with keeping an eye on all the small things that to some may not matter but in my case they make a huge change to my daily routine. Strides, I even tried some other apps but must be honest - you are the best. Simple yet motivating. Thank you! 

2020: It’s not been long since I started to use the app but so far so... amazing! :) I was looking for an app that would help me keep an eye on what is it that I’m working on right now and if I’ve done it or not. Rather bad memory doesn’t help me either!!! So this app is very helpful for me! title: My favorite app - changed my life
body:
I can’t recommend this app enough. I never write reviews, but truly this app is helping me change my life, bit by bit, day by day. 

The design is thoughtful. The app allows flexibility in terms of category, naming, and metrics so that you can customize things for the precise habit or goal you’re working towards. Even with all the flexibility the app is still functional and doesn’t have superfluous features that make it clunky like some other apps I’ve seen in this category. 

I have the paid version for one year and will probably update to the lifetime version when my subscription ends. The free version is great too, but I wanted more customization. It was a great investment in myself and improving my life.

title: Latest Update has destroyed half of the utility of this app
body:
You latest update notes say that you’ve tried to modernise the app - in actuality you’ve ruined the aesthetics as well as essentially deleting half of my data.

For example you no longer appear to be counting day in which a habit hasn’t been logged as a zero! If, for example, you are someone who is tracking total and average mileage for running, this throws off weekly/monthly averages. It also make the data far harder to read in the app; if this is modern (it isn’t) then I want no part in it.

I feel as though you’ve stolen my money by changing your service and essentially deleting my data. If these changes aren’t reversed then I will be taking my money to one of your competitors and I will be suggesting to several friends who I brought to this platform to do the same.

body:

The market for these habit apps is quite crowded due to their simplicity.

I would rather go to a different app that doesn’t ask me to go premium straight away. This is because I’m not just trying an app, I’m trying a change in my lifestyle. A change in lifestyle that I don’t know whether it will work or not, so the less commitment the better. (I guess you could also market the premium as ‘people who pay for the app are x times more likely to achieve their goals’, I still wouldn’t have signed up for it in the first 5 minutes of setting up the app though...)

title: Very useful
body:
This is so good, one of the few apps I think I will pay for. 

I’ve really gotten out of routine during the Covid lockdown, so thought I would use this to get back on track. 

It really is good, you can use it to build up good habits, reduce or limit bad habits or things bad for you. For example drink water 4 times a day.  Don’t eat more than 4 packets of crisps a week! Go to bed before 11am every night. Lol 

The goals can be set daily, weekly, monthly or averaged out. 

It’s not advertised for this purpose, but it could also be used as a reminder to take medication (as multiple reminders through the day can be set for the same item).

Or even as a task or to do list, with daily, weekly, monthly reminders set.  In fact get this and it could replace several of your other apps entirely!

 Plus it has a note section which could actually be used as a well being diary for each item you set.  Ie bad habits, you could explain to yourself why you had more than 4 packets of crisps that week! Plus you can set your own messages. So when it reminds you to drink water - you can add, because my doctor told me! 

It would be better though if different types of tagged items were displayed in different colours, with the option of grouping them together.  I see the list can be reordered but a group function would be better.  

It could also do with some clearer instructions as it took me a few goes to set up a tag title and work out how to re-order the items.

title: Too many subjects not enough time?
body:
This app is so useful for getting organised. It may seem like an overstatement to say it's changed my life but it really has. Between my work and let's be honest relaxing time I never found enough hours to complete all my studies this app really is great for building habits and it's so easy to stick to them.

A good tip for anyone using this is build a habit at a time in which you know you'll always be free to do it and nothing will impede it. For me unfortunately that's the middle of the night 1am, 2am etc. Hopefully yours aren't as late, in any case if you build a habit at a time when you'll always be free to do it you'll be amazed at how easy it is to stick to it and how much you get done. 1 hour a day of a subject over a period of time is much more rewarding than one day of cramming a subject. Excellent for getting rid of bad habits as well. 

Only issue is sometimes when editing a habit it takes a while to update properly.

title: Still buggy! It's a shame really.
body:
I bought the app before it was updated. It was buggy and kept crashing all the time. This has not changed, in fact it's worse; a lot worse. 

I'm running the app on an iPhone 6. 

Problems: (yes, I've tried deleting and restarting my phone many times) 

Still crashes when adding a tracker, or just randomly crashes. Random crashes happen a lot, even so that I've stopped using the app. The is basically unusable. 

Sometimes when adding a new tracker, it syncs to server and keeps adding multiple versions of the same tracker to the dashboard. 

I bought the app before the update and I'm being told that I will have to pay for a subscription, which with the apps performance I really wouldn't recommend or intend to do. To be honest, to buy the app, then pay for subscription, and provide terrible service and user experience is insulting. 

App animations/transitions are jarring. Not smooth at all. 

Really slow boot up time

I personally find the app quite ugly, this is exacerbated by the poor animations. 

I wanted to love this app as it's possible to track many data types. No other app does this and that's what makes this app so frustrating. If you can forgive it for its bugginess and poor looks, then it's ok. I believe the app looks the way it does as it has to allow for disparate data types, most other apps in this area have very nice looking dashboards for example. 

The idea behind the app is excellent, a one stop place to track various things you want change. Sadly the execution is rather poor. Hopefully, I'll be able to change my review once the app has been updated again.

title: Buruk👎🏻Jangan membeli aplikasi ini!
body: There have been numerous updates since my complaint, but synchronization between devices still doesn't work properly—the developers are ignoring our feedback and do not seem to care about user convenience. Aplikasi ini sangat buruk. Semua ulasan positif ditulis oleh pengembangnya sendiri. Tidak mungkin untuk mengatur pelacak untuk interval tertentu, misalnya dari 4 hingga 12 Agustus, untuk minum probiotik sekali sehari. Aplikasi yang dirancang dengan buruk ini hanya memungkinkan pengaturan tanggal mulai (saya mengatur 4 Agustus), tetapi saya tidak dapat mengatur tanggal akhir (11 Agustus). Aplikasi ini tidak cocok untuk pelacakan kebiasaan. Pengembang mengabaikan keluhan pengguna. Sinkronisasi antar perangkat tidak berfungsi. Jika Anda membuat pelacak di satu perangkat, itu tidak muncul di perangkat lain. Selain itu, jika Anda menandai pelacak sebagai selesai di satu perangkat, notifikasi tidak hilang di perangkat lain, dan Anda harus menandai secara manual sebagai selesai di perangkat kedua juga. Sinkronisasi tidak berfungsi! Pengembang tidak peduli dengan pengguna mereka! The application is terrible. The developers ignore user complaints. Synchronization between devices doesn't work. If you create a tracker on one device, it doesn't appear on the other. Additionally, if you mark a tracker as completed on one device, the notification doesn't disappear on the other, and you have to manually mark it as completed on the second device as well. Synchronization is broken! The developers don't care about their users! Do not purchase this app! All positive reviews were written by the developer themselves. It is impossible to set up a tracker for a specific interval, for example, from August 4 to August 12, to take a probiotic once a day. This poorly designed app only allows setting a start date (I set August 4), but I was unable to set an end date (August 11). The app is not suitable for habit tracking.
author: Rammzes2

title: Tidak bagus. Glitches a lot. Dont buy it!
body: The application has a synchronization bug, where if you have already checked off a habit on one device, you still receive a reminder to mark the habit on another device. WHY? All devices should automatically acknowledge the action according to synchronization, and notifications should not be sent to other devices if it has already been marked on one of them. However, all devices will still notify you, and by marking them, you will enter duplicated or tripled notes, even though it should have been done just once. DO NOT BUY this flawed application, where developers don't care about the users and ignore feedback. And the interface looks like it's from the 1990s—boring and outdated. . Terjemahan antarmuka ke bahasa Rusia sangat buruk. Pelacak kebiasaan itu bagus, tetapi untuk mencapai tujuan keuangan, lebih baik menggunakan aplikasi keuangan. Misalnya, aplikasi "Accounting Finance" mampu tidak hanya melacaknya tetapi juga mengintegrasikannya dengan rekening bank dan analitik. A habit tracker is good, but for achieving financial goals, it's better to use a financial app. For instance, the “Accounting Finance” app is capable not only of tracking them but also of integrating them with your bank account and analytics.

title: WOW!!
body:
This app is beyond amazing!
Features that blew me away: 
1. Each category is customised according to the needs of that category. For example, to track your weight it has graphs which shows your progress. 
2. You can customise the reminders according to your needs and can also set multiple reminders like 8 reminders to drink water distributed throughout the day (you can add how many ever you like). 
3. You can set goal streaks. For example, if you want to keep 30 days streak of studying, unless you complete the task it will not count it as a day. It’ll remind you the next day to complete even the previous day’s tasks.

No other habit tracker apps have so many features that too for free! I wanted to support them by paying for the premium version but it’s out of my budget. :(

title: Good concept, but too much nagging
body:
This app is really gorgeous, and it has all the features I'd want in such an app. 

My gripes about it is that:

- it is too tedious to log anything else than today (to much pushing and scrolling),

- not possible to have a general alert that you should do today's logging. I have all notifications coming at the same time, and that makes my phone go bananas with sound,

- each time you log anything, a modal dialog will pop up saying you have met your goal (independent of if you actually met your goal or not), with the possibility to share on Facebook and so on. I'm not on Facebook, but this modal dialog is not something I can tolerate in an app,

- I think it should be possible to log directly from the dashboard. If you track just 4 things, you'll push a lot of buttons to get through them all. 

If those items were given a second consideration, I'd definitely give it another chance.

Among the weaker students (though not among the good ones), monthly planning led to much bigger improvements in grades than did the daily planning. Monthly planners also kept it up much longer than the daily planners, and the continued planning thus was more likely to carry over into their work after the program ended. A year after the program ended, the monthly planners were still getting better grades than the daily planners, most of whom by this point had largely abandoned planning, daily or otherwise.” This app really helps me to set monthly goals. title: Useless for free users
body:
**SUMMARY**
This is a great app, but the premium is way too expensive, and without it you’re only able to use one tracker. If you don’t feel like dishing out $80 to use this app properly, don’t bother downloading it. 

**FULL REVIEW**
This is a brilliant app, and I really like all the options and customizations available. One of the best habit trackers I’ve come across. However, it’s close to useless now if you don’t have the premium version, which is ridiculously expensive for an app of this caliber. Before, I was able to operate 3 habits/trackers at the same time, and the app worked great. The free version suited me just fine. But now you only get one habit/tracker for free which is just plain unhelpful. No one has just one habit they need to track. This wouldn’t be as much of a problem if the premium wasn’t so expensive. The app developers may hope to get more people to purchase subscriptions because of the stark limitations of the free version, but I think they underestimate the amount of people willing to pay that much money for something that can pretty easily be done on paper. If anything, I would suggest having a way cheaper lower-level premium that just unlocks more habit slots.

title: Decent app but Overpriced
body: This is a pretty nice tracking app for developing habits. However, the free version is limited to only 3 goals, so I’m on the search for a different app. I work in human services, which means I earn a low income *and* have student loan debt. $4.99/month or $79.99 for lifetime subscription seems overpriced for a few kilobytes of storage. The developers have been providing the same response for years regarding their subscription model, stating it’s sustainable. But it’s not sustainable for customers. Subscriptions add up quickly, and an individual customer only has so much income for companies to eat up each month. [“For the price of a latte” won’t work in this instance, as I (and many others) don’t have income to waste at coffee shops.] I’ve used this app for years to track various projects and habits. But I don’t rely on it by any means. Would I consider it “life-changing” and worth repeatedly carving out a piece of my income for it, or worth giving up 1-2 weeks of groceries for a lifetime subscription? No.

title: Not easy to use
body: I downloaded the app with the purpose of tracking numerous daily, weekly, monthly and annual objectives for my business. While I understand the steps to achieving goals, what I don’t understand is how to customize them with this app. For example, I want to set a goal for monthly revenue of $500,000. I want to see by the day how close my team is, by entering a figure that I receive from a daily report. I can’t figure out how to do that. Another example, I have a goal for my team to make 10 introduction calls a day. That’s 50 calls per week. I get a report, but want to log those numbers into the app myself daily, and know their progress. I’m sure this can be done. But it’s not that easy to understand how. I downloaded the “Upgrade” for 7 days with the intent to purchase the “Lifetime Subscription” and once I understand it, roll it out to my management team. The tutorials are great motivation. It would have been helpful to have some simple step by step instructions.

title: So many bugs with so much potential
body:

The problem are the bugs. The creator of this app had another app called summit. I really wanted that one to work as well. But it had similar bugs.

The first bug is, sometimes if you mark no, it won’t mark as no. I would press no, it wouldn’t do anything. And continue to mark it a habit as no. Still wouldn’t do anything. Until I check the history of the habit, and they are all listed there. Yet it never moved. 

This problem also happens when you have a habit that requires more than once a day. So let’s say you want to drink water 10 times a day, if you press no. It doesn’t do anything. 

Another problem is the Apple Watch app. It bugs out, if you press yes or no, doesn’t do anything at times. Yet it will track it on the phone.

title: Allow more than 3 habits without paying
body: I really enjoyed your layout and the construction of your app. I did quite a lot of research to pick your app out from the multiple other goal apps. I think you are unfortunately going to loose quite a few customers due to making people pay money to have more than 3 habits. Statistics may state you should only focus on a couple habits but you shouldn’t make people feel like they can’t have more than 3 unless they pay. Also, the individuals who are using an app to help organize their habits most likely need an app because they have multiple habits they need to keep track of. I would highly recommend you increasing the amount of habits before people have to pay because consumers are going to get frustrated and go to an app that doesn’t make them pay for more than 3 habits. I will pay for an app after I use it for a couple weeks and have grown to appreciate the app on a day to day basis. You are not allowing a certain group of people try out your app for a couple weeks for free if they have more than 3 habits so they will delete it immediately. At least let people track more habits so they can grow to appreciate your app before they have to pay.

title: Reality Check  Goal App
body:
Like anything new it takes a minute to find your flow with it. My impatient self included. Not Because it’s complicated. It’s actually a simple app to work your goals. I reworked my goals  8 times my first week because what I thought I could accomplish in one day and then repeat that pace 5 days in a row was over zealous. 
Strides show you clearly what you’re day looks like in reality. I didn’t even have time schedule to take a piss. I was so ridiculously over confident with what was humanly possible to accomplish in a day. 
strides forces you to look at what you want to accomplish and once you write it out you’ll see if it’s possible to work towards your goal at that pace. 
It’s hard to cut things out of your day when your so enthusiastic about accomplishing a goal….. but doing it for a week and quitting is worse than tampering down  your daily reality and still  doing something consistent per day towards your objective. 
Too, the customer service is great. 
Get after it!

title: Responsive developer and great app
body:
I found the app to be very useful in how it allows you to define multiple types of goals. This app complements the goalsetting course very well.

In the past few days I started seeing an issue where goals would get duplicated leading to an erratic behavior in the app. I reached out to the developer, and within a day the developer emailed me back with a solution. The app is now functioning perfectly and I’m already seeing changes in my behavior which is really the purpose of any good habits or goal setting app.

While generally I’m not a fan of subscriptions, the pricing for this app is reasonable considering what it delivers and the level of commitment and support from developer. 

The app provides the necessary features that allow you sticking to your goals. This includes: notifications which are highly customizable, monitoring of trends and progress, easy shortcuts, easy recording of progress, and many other features.

Things I would like to see are improved fonts especially in widgets that will allow you to see all of your goals at a glance. Currently the fonts are too large and I’m only able to view about half of my goals.This requires me to go into the app each time instead of quickly recording progress via widget.

Overall this is a great app, probably one of the best goalsetting apps I’ve seen on the App Store so far. I’m looking forward to many new features that are streamlined in the recording, the monitoring, and the tracking of progress.

title: Versatility and SMART goals
body: This review is for the subscription version of the app. After a few days of trying it for free, I was hooked. I have never before rated an app voluntarily before being asked by the app. This app is amazing and has proven to be extraordinarily productive for me, especially as someone with diagnosed ADHD. For those who may not know, SMART goals = specific, measurable, achievable, realistic, and time-limited. This app is like the to-do list I always wanted. Not only does it allow me to set goals and objectives, it also gives me several ways of looking at my data. It keeps me on track and I’ve been able to see tangible results. The flexibility comes in because it allows you to play around with all aspects of the SMART goals. For example, I’m reminding myself to drink water because I usually don’t unless there’s coffee or tea in it. I’m keeping track of my weight with an ultimate weight goal that I’ve selected on the date that I’ve selected. I’m keeping track of the things I eat so that I can develop more healthy patterns of eating by setting goals. I’m completing a project at home that I’ve literally been neglecting for years. The app gives me information about how I’m doing after I set my parameters and report my progress. I’m keeping track of the professional reading I’m doing because I’m able to reinforce this behavior as well as other behaviors that I’m cultivating. You get the idea. The other thing that I like about this app, which may be a minor detail, is that it does not include “cute“ graphics. The app has all the graphics you need presented in a straightforward and readable manner. Finally, there are numerous predefined trackers under multiple categories, but you also have the option of creating your own. The only additional feature I can think of would be to be able to set a tracker that included a timer for doing a particular task; for example, doing something that you don’t like, but you know that you need to do, for 15 minutes or 30 minutes per day for that task with an alarm at the end. But that’s not a dealbreaker in anyway because I can already do that on the iPhone. Wait! One more thing: the developer also makes available tutorials on setting goals. This is what tipped me over the edge and made me come here to write this review. You will not regret subscribing to this app. The end and thank you!

I think it takes a specific personality type to respond well to this sort of app, but thankfully I like achieving goals and checking things off lists so I do well ☺️

title: Great app (amazing widget) with flaws
body:
I tried like every single habit app on my new iPad, and settled on this one.

The widget that you offer is by far the most aesthetic, with just the right amount of info. I set habit counts for a week... for example, exercise 3 times a week. You show how many exercises I have overall, how many more I need to complete, you show how many weeks of streaks I have, if I missed my last week streak, you show ALL my habits, you clear things from the board when I tick them off, you have reminders of course. All this with iPadOS dashboard docking means I see my habits every time I use my iPad, and get all the information and functionality I need from the home screen. That’s amazing and I’ll keep using the app for that.

There are bugs with that widget though. Sometimes it doesn’t update quick enough. Sometimes it shows “unable to load” or is completely blank. Sometimes random habits will appear there with some black color and just have the text “label” on them. Hopefully you can fix these issues. Overall though this app is helping me get my life together. Please keep maintaining that widget and keep it high quality. I know some people say “oh who cares about the widget” but it’s a lot of us. Please don’t axe it, or forget about it!

Edit: oh, one thing. Some tasks can only be done at a certain time. Lets pretend that’s “be in bed by 8” or “brush your teeth before bed”. There’s no way to clear my list so that I don’t see this all day. It would be nice if I could pick a single trigger time for my tasks on when to show them. If I happen to wake up at 3am, I’m not going to workout, but maybe I can fulfill a “charge my ipad” habit or other habits.

title: Great app, UI could use work
body:
For the longest time I had a separate list for habits in my Reminders app, but I hated that I couldn’t see the progress I’d been making on my habits. Then began my search for the best habit tracker on the App Store.

I’ve tried Productive, Habit, Done, Fabulous, Streaks, a few other mediocre apps, and finally Strides. I have to say as far as usability goes, Strides is far above the rest. You get the sense that this is a team that keeps up with the latest trends and pushes updates constantly.

One area where I think it falls behind is in general appearance. Specifically, I’d love it if the UI was more differentiated from the Apple Reminders app, which I already use a ton, and was more focused on showing you how far you’ve progressed in the last week. “Done”, “Habit”, and “Streaks” all do a really good job of this with beautiful interfaces, but they lack the functionality of Strides.

“Fabulous” was pretty annoying as an app, but I think one thing it does well is offering motivational paths and programs. I think if small things like this were more closely integrated into the Strides it would feel a little more friendly and optimistic. Maybe let people write motivational quotes in each tracker that would pop up when you get a notification?

Overall great app though, and my habit tracker of choice on the App Store.

title: Awesome habit/goal tracker.. one issue
body:
Love the apps functions, UI/UX. It has been pivotal in tracking my progress and staying on top of my goals. My only issue and something I think should be changed is the tagging and archive features. I love the tagging feature to organize my goals.. BUT I track daily goals tagged by their month/year and I also track my annual goals tagged as annual/year. BUT in my due today tab the daily goals that have a goal date that is in the past they still appear in the due today tab. First problem, the due today tab should only show you the items that are within the set period of time for the specific goal. For example, I have a goal that is a target number to hit for the period of January 1 -31. On February 1, that same goal was still showing up as due today. 

Second issue, to try to fix the first issue I decided to archive the goals that have “expired”, which seems to alleviate this because they no longer appear in my due today tab. BUT when I click the drop down to sort by tags, my January 2020 tag is now empty because I archived those goals. So, it should be possible to archive any and all goals but still be able to sort by their other tags. 

Would love to see a solution to this issue, whether it’s the one I described or another one. Thanks! Still absolutely love the app, just a few minor suggestions for optimization.

title: Great app, some improvements would make it perfect!
body:
This is an amazing app, it’s helped me a lot in tracking my habits. I especially love the feature of being able to quantify my habits with numbers, instead of just a yes/no option. (So for my reading habit, I can put in the number of minutes I’m reading per day and it also shows me my average, which is really helpful.)
However, I have a couple of suggestions.
1. It would be awesome if the “best streak” statistic would show up for numerical/quantity habits too(in addition to the “current streak” stat) like it does for yes/no habits, since it gives me something to compare myself to. The same for the monthly log that can be seen in yes/no habits, (this too is absent in numerical habits)
2. It would be great if in addition to the average, it could show me total number done (so for eg: in addition to showing that my jogging average/day is 35 minutes, it also shows that jogging was done for a total of 9,000 minutes) This would were as a great motivator/confidence booster!
2. It would be helpful if I could pause/suspend habits, and skip them since some of them are seasonal/mightbbe cancelled for the week, and I don’t want my average messed up. [On a side note, the archive feature is really great for habits that you’re done with but don’t want to delete!]
Last but not least, kudos to the app developers for doing a really great job!!

title: Essential app for tracking habits, best out of many I’ve used
body:
I felt like I had to write an actual review to give this app some more support. Habit tracking apps don’t get nearly the press coverage of todo list apps, document and note apps, cloud storage apps, or even photo filter apps. This is so unfortunate, because tracking your repeated actions and adjusting them, is one of the most powerful ways to shape your life. 

I think that habits environment and identity are interwoven, and collectively determine the course of our lives. 

This app is the best I’ve found for tracking repetitions and other important quantities (besides YNAB which I use to budget, and Mynetdiary which I use for calorie tracking).

For me there are a few killer features that make Strides stand head and shoulders above all the other habit apps I’ve tried. 
- The ability to track multiple reps in the same day, which is so crucial for actually shaping the day
- A webapp that has mobile and desktop UIs, and allows Strides to be used on any device with a web browser, including my android phone. (If you’ve never tried the webapp, I def suggest you check it out. I actually have come to prefer using the webapp on the iPad because the desktop UI is simultaneously cleaner in some respects, and also easier to work with imo).
The only thing you miss it on from the webapp seems to be reminders. Not a big deal for me, as I actually tend to use apps like ticktick (best task/todo list app imo) for reminders.
- Tags. I don’t have to say much here, just look at most habit apps and notice that they don’t have a way to easily group and filter habits, other than simple color labels. That’s fine if you have only a few habits, but if you really track a lot of things that are important to your life, sooner or later you will want to group and filter the habits so you can focus on a select few. 

Love the Strides app, I’ve been a subscriber since I switched to it from habit bull (which I think is the closest to strides, but lacked the tags and the the webapp, but did at least have multi rep tracking and apps for android and iOS, the apps didn’t like to sync across iOS and android for me very well however).

title: Really really good, but...
body:
Updated: Since the developer updated their response to me, I wanted to do the same:

- Things did not require a full, brand new purchases when their last version (Things 3) came out in 2017, five years after Things 2 was released. If you had purchased the prior version you received a launch discount. This means I spent $60 for three years of support universally so far (Mac, iPad, iPhone). Saying you’ll spend $100 every few years unless you’re okay with using out of date and unsupported software is dishonest and intentionally vague to make their model look better. Strides would have cost more during the current timeframe alone. 
- Fantastical 1 came out in 2011, and Fantastical 2 was released in 2015. They both cost $5 for iPhone and $10 for iPad, meaning Strides was once again more for that amount of time. It would have been another $50 for macOS, but still cheaper than Strides as it’s been FOUR YEARS since Fantastical 2 came out. 
- Things 3 is a full blown, in depth task and project management system. Strides is a habit tracking app. Plenty of habit apps cost much less than Strides as a one time payment, even if they don’t have as many features. To compare Strides to Things is a false equivalency as habit apps are not as complex or necessary as task/project management. 

I understand your pricing model, as I pay for plenty of subscriptions - for instance, Bear is $15/year for universal device support and does much more than Strides. Thanks for trying to explain everything to me, and best of luck to you as well. However your subscription pricing is beyond agreeable. 

————

This app is great, it really is. BUT you're limited to only ten trackers. Okay, if you're a power user then you have to expect to pay for features, and this app is definitely worth money... Just not $5/month or $40/year! Why can't I spend $10-$20 to just unlock the features forever? I know you guys need to make money but no software is worth $40/year, period. Even professional apps only charge once. I'm looking for another app/way to track until the price comes down.

Edit: I appreciate a response from you, and taking the time to write up a detailed and thorough explanation. I currently use Things 3, I've purchased OmniFocus, Fantastical 1&2, Scriviner on macOS and iOS.... The list goes on. They don't charge any monthly or yearly subscriptions and have the same features. I don't claim to know a ton about app monetization or running a business, but other apps with just as much (if not more) production value seem to be able to do it. Again, thanks for responding, and I wish you guys the best, but I'm going back to using Persistence (unless you guys make some changes, of course). Thanks again!

Second Edit: Can I just say how cool it is, regardless of your opinion on this discussion, that the CEO is actually taking the time to respond to customer reviews in a thoughtful manner? Other devs won't say a word. Kudos for that. I really appreciate it. Shout out to the financial app DashFlow, also made by this company. I am a paying customer to that subscription service.

I recommend others either buy WAY OF LIFE (NO subscriptions another +) or keep your habits in a spreadsheet.

title: Unfortunate limiting subscription model
body: Probably one of my favorite productivity, habit-tracking apps I've tried.  Moreover, the app is intuitive and I feel like it has been well tested for user experience. However, I don't agree with justification for a subscription model, as posted by the app author.  The subscription is supposed to pay for hosting services, but I don't see why I need to pay for hosting? Simply save my data locally or offer connection to cloud service (i.e. dropbox) if users really want to sync.  (For example, 1password has a subscription model, but offers a lifetime license for $60). I know plenty of people who would have used this app if it was a simple one-time purchase.  In my opinion as a fellow developer, tracker apps are not difficult to build, and it is only a matter of time a more affordable app similar to strides will enter the market - I would love to support this if it made more sense than subscribing so you can "sync".   Would be happy to pay a legitimate software license price for it, it is clearly worth more than a $10 app.  Thanks though, hope you will take it into consideration.

title: Bugs out when you change time zones?
body: So far, this was the best habit tracker I found that gave me 7 habits without having to pay sub fees >.< anyway, I was finding the app pretty awesome but then I went from the pacific time zone to the eastern time zone on holiday and all streaks and checks got completely messed up! I didn’t understand what was going on so I went back through time and rechecked days that had previously been checked but I couldn’t remember everything for what I did on what days. title: The subscription fee is insane!
body: I’ve already read the creator’s response regarding the reasoning behind the subscription vs. a one-time cost. This app is great - but most people that are working on improving habits would like to work on more than 7. I promoted this app for a while on my productivity social media platform, but kept getting that same feedback from followers, and I do agree with them. If the ability to sync across platforms is causing an expensive subscription, perhaps there could be an option with one-time payment that simply allows users to have more goals? The other “perks” that the subscription includes to try to defend its $30/year price tag are nice, but the majority would agree they aren’t proportionally useful. When you look at other apps in this space - Things 3, for example - that cost significantly less (and do not rehire a subscription) and do significantly more in terms of achieving increased productivity, it makes you wonder what the issue is here. I am always more than happy to pay plenty for an app when the value is there, but it’s just not here in this case.

title: Well planned, I find myself saying ‘Aha!’

I made the goal by choosing to track numbers instead of a habit. I wasn’t getting into the studio as often as I liked so I made a new goal by choosing to track it as a habit and that gives you a little calendar graphic which the other trackers don’t have. You can’t change a goal type once you’ve made it but you can make a new one. Otherwise, all sorts of other settings in each goal are changeable as you go along. Everything shows streaks, averages and if you’ve met your goal or not for the given period.  Then, you can even set a goal for streaks, so that’s another layer of consistency tracking. I had to read a little and play with it a little, but I like it and subscribed for a year. I use it with Trello which I use as a broader idea and task tracking pinboard.

title: Keep Motivation Simple with Strides
body:
Strides daily goals appear as simple category titles under bad and good habit types.  Stop feeling like a felon by listing everything as a positive daily goal you KNOW you can meet or exceed. 

Select the prebuilt Strides category name and easy template, changing the name or building you own goal title or category of related mini-steps. Each daily goal can represent a single number, a yes/no action, a time period, a project, or a cluster of tiny actions you do or stop doing.  

The process is fun, flexible, strongly motivating, and simple enough to be sustainable.  Track and graph your actions for as long as you want, adding notes for related choices, modifications, reactions.  

Freely edit or delete goals if you feel overwhelmed.  Select single or multiple timed daily reminders if you like until habits form. Reorder your list of daily goals whenever you want. You’ll end up checking off your successes all day long. Sweet! 👍

title: I Have Narrowed My Choices To Two
body:
After examining about a dozen habit tracking apps, there are two contenders left: Strides and another app.  I was surprised at how fast I was able to reject most of them.

Strides, as well as the other, comes with features I consider important.  Namely, syncing across devices, the ability to set reminders for particular habits, and integration with Apple Watch.

One feature that Strides has but the other does not is the ability to manage my data on a website.  I would prefer an app for macOS but neither of the two apps offers that.

There are a couple of gotchas.  The first regards syncing.  Few will ever see this.  I have a tendency to close apps on my devices immediately after using them.  If I change some settings on some habits using my iPad and close the app before it has a chance to sync and make some changes using my iPhone, those changes will get overwritten the next time I use the app on the iPad.  The other app overcomes this condition by forcing me to press a save button when I am done making changes at which time it syncs those changes.

The second gotcha regards the option to stop syncing.  It doesn’t just stop syncing.  It deletes my account.  I find this a very odd naming convention.  I think I should be able to stop syncing without deleting my account.  My data is important to me and it should be protected.  I encourage the developer to rectify this.

Finally, this is a subscription based app and it costs $40 per year.  That’s pretty expensive when I compare it to a subscription based task manager app that charges $20 per year.  I find it difficult to justify the cost.

My current trackers are: 
>Workouts (to tally them yearly)
>meditate (5/week)
>Journaling (2/week)
>Awake by 8 (5/week)
>stomach feel (1-10): a subjective measurement of how my stomach is doing
>sleep quality (1-10): a subjective measurement of how well I slept

Many times I forget to log but it doesn’t matter. I log when I remember to log.

One thing I would add though is some celebration when you reach your goals. Like optional balloons on the screen or something.

title: Well thought out, great for tracking progress!
body:
This is a great app for tracking your progress on you habits. Ever since all the great updates recently created this year, the app is among the best planning tools. Personally, I prefer to use my physical paper planning tools for this sort of stuff, but the format of the app makes it worth it. It gives a clean view of your progress and an easy way to track it. The last great part for me is that it keeps me accountable. I cringe each time I have to mark a "No" for my habit that day, and it motivates me to do it. 

Being a teenager in high school, normally I NEVER take the time to write a review for something. This is only the third thing I have ever reviewed on the Internet, and it's only if I find something incredible. 

If you actually use this app for real, and go out and do the work, you can develop very successful goal setting habits. Don't wait for New Years Eve to start. START TODAY! Go out all accomplish your goals! Strides can help you do that if you willing to put in the work and dedicate yourself. However, remember that even the best of productivity tools can't make you productive if you don't go out there in real life and crank out that workout or whatever your trying to do. 

Thank you Strides for the great app!

title: A seriously powerful app
body:
I started using this app only 5 days ago, but it’s already making huge differences in my life. I feel that, because of this app, I can really start achieving the goals I’ve been wanting to achieve. This might sound gross, but I’ve always struggled to make sure to brush and floss my teeth twice a day. Since using this app, I haven’t missed it once. I’ve started getting back into reading by setting a daily goal of reading an hour a day. I’ve made sure to be working out at least 5 days a week because of this app. I’ve started journaling at the end of each day because of this app. I’ve set weight goals for myself that I’m tracking, and it even gives a projection for my weight by my goal date based on how much progress I’m making so far. 

The app is basically just a daily to-do list, and that may sound super simple, but it’s so powerful. I feel accomplished completing my goals each day, and the app encourages me to stick with it and achieve more. Thanks to Strides, I’m able to form the habits I’ve been wanting to form, and break my goals up into pieces each day, which makes them much easier to achieve. I really just want to say thank you to the developers for helping me better myself and better my life. I highly recommend this for anyone looking to do the same.

title: Sleek, Simple Strides
body:
So I downloaded several different apps of this type of goal-tracker app.  I was able to quickly narrow it down to this and one other by virtue of how easy it is to add custom goals and track them.  Over the coarse of a month this one has become by far my favorite.  It allows me to customize what, how many, how often,and track with an easy swipe left or right.  It gives me reminders but doesn't annoy me.  I can easily go back to log days I've done (or not) but haven't logged and I can see at a glance whether I'm improving the frequency of my goals.  This has quickly become one of my most frequently used apps!  Highly recommend for all ages of goal-setters and (hopefully) accompish-ers!  
Update:  I’ve been using this for about six months now and still think this is by far the best goal-tracker app.  I love the personalized goals and being able to look back over the months and see how I’m improving long-term.  I’m slowly adding goals and know this app is what is keeping me focused!

title: Well Designed and Intuitive
body:
I am one of the apps free users. This is a well designed and intuitive goal tracking app. Very simple to use but with nice customizations. I had used it for a few months this spring, and was really building some great new habits, when I fell out of use for unrelated reasons. I jumped back into the app this fall and am truly amazed about how the awareness and mindfulness of regular goal tracking motivates me to move towards my goals. 

I really am puzzled by how quickly I started flossing, getting up earlier, and reading more books once I started using the app again which were goals that didn’t change between spring and summer. 

I currently track 9 goals, and am allowed 10 total free. I enter my progress in the morning and evenings for my daily goals and weekly goals. My longer term goals I enter an update when there is something related to them. I like the way they present my progress. Thanks Strides Team!

title: Buggy!
body:

I travel often, internationally as well as domestically, and there are lots of bugs that relate to the alerts and time zone settings that are causing a lot of frustration. There are consistent anomalies, but for one example, I've just returned to the east coast of the US from the west coast and I the alerts are all thrown off by three hours. I've gone into the time zone settings and it indicates that I am in EST, but the alerts on one of my goals is alerting at the wrong time. If I go into the goal directly and try and update the alert time, it won't keep the time that I've selected, it reverts back to the previous time that is three hours off. 

Attempting to manually adjust the time zone doesn't work either, the check next to the time zone doesn't change when another time zone is selected.

The synchronization across devices is off as well. If I change a goal setting for one goal it often doesn't update on the other device. 

These bugs are frustrating.

title: Amazing App. Still could use some work.
body:
First off, a huge thanks to the developer who took the time to respond to my last review. That is a sign of good customer service.
And now, on with my updated review: I've tried several apps like this one, and Strides is by far the best. It does almost everything I need it to, almost meaning I would like to be able to make notes in this app, but I'm too cheap to pay several dollars a month to unlock the rest of the features, so I'll just make my notes in a different app. The developer said it is possible to add notes to logs for free, but I can't figure out how to do that and they didn't give instructions, so hopefully another developer will respond to this review and let me know how that works. I like how this app lets you make and track different types of goals. Right now, I have one project with different milestones that I can track my progress of percentage wise and check them off when they are done. I also have a goal set to write for an hour a day that I can enter numerical amounts for to see if I go over or under my goal, and the keeps a running average, streak count, and success rate so I can see how I am doing. Strides does a lot more than this, but this is what I have discovered so far.
Now that I've been using it for a while, I've noticed one majorly annoying problem. When you create a new project in the app, it divides the weight of the milestones evenly, but if you want to create new milestones to an already existing project, it doesn't divide the percent weight of each milestone evenly, and I have to go in and alter the percentages manually. Due to the nature of the projects I use this for, I don't have a way of knowing the exact number of milestones from the very beginning. I usually end up needing to add or subtract milestones. This is a smart phone. They are good at math. There should be a button you can press that automatically divides the percentages to account for the new milestones you add. Even if the developers don't make a button to do this automatically, they need to make the app smart enough to have percentages with decimals so I can divide it exactly evenly myself. Also, when I am viewing my progress for the day, there is the chart with the line saying where I should be that day. This line should also include what percent I should be at. I can usually guesstimate, but I would prefer an exact number.  One last problem, this app also has a computer version. When I started a new project, I decided to start it on the computer version because I could type the names of all the milestones faster that way. However, when I went over to the app after doing this, the milestones I had added on the computer were out of order, and some were missing altogether. If there is going to be a web version and a mobile version, there needs to be continuity. The developer said that this was due to the fact that the web version is still a beta version, so I'm hoping they fix this by the time the beta version becomes an actual version. Overall, this is an excellent app, and it will be even better with more tweaking.
Update: I've noticed that the line saying what percentage I'm supposed to be at moves throughout the day. It would be better if it went directly to the target percentage each day instead of moving. There have been times when I think I'm on target for the day, but when I go back to it a few hours later, it shows that I am behind. Also, there needs to be a way of not including certain days of the week in the graph showing where you need to be in a project. You can choose to only have the app remind you to make logs on certain days, but with projects, the days you don't log are still calculated into the graph showing where you need to be each day. I generally don't work on weekends, so when I go back to my project on Monday, I sometimes find that I am drastically behind, and I have to frantically play catch up. I try to stay ahead on my projects, but it would be better if the app would automatically leave certain days out rather than me having to manually determine how much extra work I have to do each day so I don't fall behind when the weekend comes around and the target line on the app jumps ahead on me. That may make me sound lazy, but the whole point of this app is to make tracking projects more convenient, so the features of the app should be convenient.

title: Works Even For Motivated Folks
body:
After a year of distractions and stalling on a project, I had to do something to combat the intimidating size of it and approaching deadline. I thought 'there must be an app to help with this'. Checked into Strides. I will say it's not 'immediately' intuitive on all counts but with the tiniest bit of tinkering you get it. I've been able to do in two weeks what I couldn't in a year. I don't watch tv and am very self motivated but this project of mine had some failure fears attached to it. After a year of struggle needed some help. 

  — I sat first with pen and paper. Worked backward from my deadline and split my project into phases, and then further into weekly tasks. I put this info into the app. And VOILA! 

  — If in your life you've been a list person.... enjoying the checking-off of things, then this app is for you. 

  — After each task completed I go into Strides and click on the bell icon, slide the bar to my progress point and the red turns to green. Ahhhh, I'm caught up for the day and a lovely green check mark appears. I have many months of work ahead toward my goal, and finally looking forward to it!

title: Weak Product
body:
Update: 
I did get access to the iPad subscription after contacting the help desk. The subscription was not valid for the iPhone version. I keep getting an alert to pay an extra $40 for iPhone access to the full program. 

The goals show up on both the iPhone and iPad, but the updates do not transfer between the devices. 

Also, I did figure out how to change the categories: you can modify with the full price version.

Original review:
I purchased the annual subscription but never got access to the full app. So, it's a rip-off to start. 

There are very few categories to choose from. So, if you're a person who operates beyond the goals for your weight, income, etc., you're out of luck with that function. It's just not a very flexible or functional product if you have an ounce of originality.

All good goals are measurable. This app, however, severely limits the metrics you can choose. For example, if your goal is to drink water, you're stuck with choosing the number of times per day you want to drink (as opposed to, say, setting a goal to drink 1 gallon a day). You have to be very willing to compromise your goals just to make the app work.

The app is not able to track the amount of time that you did something. For example, you can check that you exercised, but you can't track how many minutes you exercised. Walking up a flight of stairs has as much significance as a day-long hike in this app.

I think the only way to reset it is to delete the goal and start a new one, which would delete all the data I did log.

title: Everyting you could need
body:
I don't usually take the time to write reviews, but I'm too pleased with this app not to. I've gone through a variety of ways to track both habits (flossing, brief bouts of intense physical exercise, etc) and goals (completing a series of online courses, piano practice), but Strides has made it super simple. It just works; it's flexible enough to allow you dictate exactly what your habits and goals look like without making it overwhelming, and it all it takes is a quick daily glance to see how you're doing.

I had purchased Strides Plus on my iPad and it didn't sync across to my iPhone. I emailed support, and literally within 20 minutes they had taken care of the problem. This is truly one of those apps that deserves your attention and investment, and you get a whole ton out of it even with the free version. Kudos to the Strides team.

body:
I’ve been using it for 3 types of tracking:
- keep track of my good habits, e.g. exercise 5x per week, play my instrument 4x, …. It’s super easy to log an entry, and I like the simple feedback for being on track 
- you can also use it to keep track of bad habits, e.g don’t drink/snack more than x times a week. I find strides very simple for tracking such things. You can specify it’s a negative habit so that it displays differently than “positive” habits
- keep track of project deadlines. This is useful for things I want to do but aren’t super urgent. I can set deadlines far enough in the future that I can keep my mind clear but know I’ll be reminded.

title: Good for tracking but maybe not setting
body:
UPDATE: 
After using this app for a week I have to downgrade to 3 stars. I will be going back to Brain Tracy's Goal Wizard. There are too any issues with Strides right now. 

It doesn't work in landscape on the iPad. 

When you have a goal with milestones you can add more than 4 milestones but when you tap on the dashboard to show them you can only see 4. I understand many goals have sequential milestones so this might not be a problem for some but I have many parallel milestones for my work objectives. 

I don't like mixing habits and goals. These are two different things and shouldn't be mixed (in my opinion obviously). 

Milestones tracking is simply a matter of sliding a percentage done slider. I would rather have tasks per milestone and have the percentage complete calculated. This is a preference and not a bug in the program but the purpose of these apps is to help us achieve goals so I would like it to help break down goals better so I can focus on doable tasks. 

ORIGINAL REVIEW:
Strides has a nice clean interface and is nice to track habits. They have combined tracking habits and goals which are two very different things. I think some people might like consolidating everything into one app. 

But for goal tracking, it lacks a feature almost all goal tracking apps lack. How to determine your goals. This seems like a simple thing but it's actually rather difficult and requires a lot of thought. Here's an example. 

Someone says they have a goal of owning a boat. I might start by asking why? Well, I can enjoy with my friends.  Ok, what if you didn't have your friends on the boat. Well, it wouldn't be as fun. I see, so what is making you happy is doing something fun with friends? I guess, but it would really fun on a boat. True, but list some of the negatives of a boat too. Well, it's expensive to buy and maintain. You have to worry when a bad storm is coming. So maybe you can think of some alternatives. Perhaps take boating lessons and join a boat club where you don't own a boat?

Anyway, the point is it takes a lot of thought to clarify your goals. They should be written down and placed in a context of what's important in your life. You can do this outside this app and then add the goals to the app but you still need this step. There are some apps that focus on selecting the correct goals but I haven't found one that is perfect yet. Perhaps preparing on paper then tracking with this app is a good way to go. 

I would bump this up to 5 stars if there was a way to associate tasks to milestones. Perhaps tie it to tasks in the Reminders app.

body:

I bought and paid for this app before it was converted to a subscription based app. I liked it even though it was completely incapable of calculating basic math due to faulty assumptions about data. (Hint: if someone wants to track 30 minutes of guitar practice every day each week, the calculation needs to treat days without a log as having a zero value. It's REALLY basic math.)

Well, I didn't update my apps for a long time and what did I discover upon updating? The app is now a subscription fee, and incredibly expensive considering what it does.

Normally I'm not so condescending, but I'm really upset that I spent $5 on this app and now the developer has disabled it on my device because they got greedy and decided they now must get $5 per month. 

Sorry. You still can't do basic math, you don't get $5 per month.

Pathetic.

title: Goodbye Strides… This is not the way to do business
body:
I loved Strides. I downloaded it last summer (back when it was free) and had set-up dozens of goals. I used the app regularly and recommended it to others in person and on my website (which reaches around 70K people each month). In other words, I was a fan.

Then, just yesterday I noticed that there was an update for the app. I scanned through the list of improvements and bug fixes and thought everything looked good. I downloaded the update.

This morning I opened the app to check my progress on reaching my goals and was asked to create an account — which I had never been asked to do before. But I didn’t begrudge Strides this request because, after all, I was a fan.

I created my account and was then walked through a tutorial on how to use the app. This created a sense of foreboding in me, especially when the app offered to help me “get started” with creating goals. I already had over a dozen goals in progress. I didn’t need help setting up new ones.

By the time I finished the tutorial my fears were confirmed. The new “test” goal I had created was the only goal listed in the app. All of my data and progress had been erased — and there at the bottom of the menu was the message:

“29 of 30 days remaining in your free trial.”

I’m sorry, Pure Signal. You’ve created a great app. You certainly deserve to get paid for it. And you probably should have asked people to create accounts right from the beginning.

But you can’t trick loyal, existing customers into giving up their free version of the app by hiding a subscription service in an update. And you can’t erase all their data and expect them to start over from scratch and pay for the privilege.

You’ve left a really bad taste in my mouth.

title: Versatile and Capable app, excellent service
body:
This is a great app. I have been using it for several months and have been happy with it.  There were a few bugs initially, but as I reported them, I was contacted by the Strides team with a reason  why the bug happened and what their plan was to address it. I was surprised by this 1-on-1 communication and was very pleased that the team reviews and addresses customer feedback.  When the 3.0 version came, along with the pricing scheme change, the app had a rough couple months. As an early adopter, I was guaranteed a free subscription which I was happy with. However, due to a bug, after the free, trial period ended, I was locked out of the app. I was quite annoyed so I decided to find a new app. After a long search and trying 7-10 other apps (Lift, Good Habits, Way of Life, Loggr, Balanced, Momentum, Full, Daily Tracker, just to name a few) I found that there wasn't an app that does what Strides does. Here's what I mean: I want to track Yes/No goals (wake up early, don't eat sugar, etc) and there are several apps that do that. But I also want to track continuous data (how many pounds did I lose this week, how many pages did I read today) and there are several apps that do that. But Strides is the only app that I have found that allows me to do both. I can have all sorts of habit types and Strides tracks them all. After my search for a replacement came up empty, I reached out to the Strides team about being locked out and they promptly addressed the issue and I'm back using the app. 

So overall, the app is versatile and capable of tracking multiple types of data and goals, and the Strides team provides great support.  I would recommend the app. Not sure about the pricing scheme but since I purchased it early on, I'm not worried about that.

title: Nice app, good interface, needs small tweaks
body: Lot of people seem to be asking for a lot, and I think the goal of this app is to keep things simple.  It needs to be simple enough to be usable for a variety of purposes, and its doing that well.  My reason for the three stars is because of a few minor issues.  The Dashboard is nice, but needs to be cleaned up Apple Style. Now its a list with a 1/4 or 1/6 or something like that. I think the screen should be a quick glance to show where you are on your various tasks (green, yellow and red colors on some sort of bar would be good).  Those I complete should automatically sort to the bottom - if I have 16 items I am tracking I have to go back and forth…there should be an option to sort the dashboard using some logic.   And the bars where it is 6/8 can be yellow instead of green vs 1/5 can be read maybe….? Its a ‘dashboard’ so needs to be designed that way.  Once I get into the item, like someone said, should have green, red and yellow or orange to show states of progress. Graphs can be longer (if I am tracking BP for a year, I can’t see it now).  Some more tracking measurements - and maybe there should be a choice of what I want on the screen for those items that I would want to track?  For some items streak or success rate may not be important but some other measurement?

title: Awesome For Building Good Habits
body:
This app is fantastic for tracking your progress and helping you hold yourself accountable for all kinda of goals you set for yourself, whether that's exercising everyday, answering all your emails by the time you go to sleep, or maintaining a positive attitude.

However, from a design perspective, there's so much going on. When I'm tracking my progress, I bounce from one graph to another, and get lost along the way. I don't mind it, but Strides should be designed to be simple to follow. I have to click several buttons to before I get to the log section.

Regardless, I love it. There's another app called Weave that helps you track your projects and reminds of them, helps you keep track of them and your possible expenses that come with it, but that too, has a lot going on. Strides is simple enough that I get to track a whole number of personal, fitness, and business goals and it's exciting to check off and track. There are just all these graphs that use more math than it needs to.

Still my every day app!

4/5

title: Where has this app been all my life?
body:
I was always taught about goals and goalsetting.  Have use the day planners since I was a teenager.  This is the first time, however, I have been given access to learn how to move through goals and reach them.  

It's all in the structuring of the goal and the feedback of the progress. I never learned this part of goalsetting. Goalsetting to me used to be an exercise of writing down wishes. Now I see that it is so much more.

This program is a solid bridge between the dream and the reality. Anyone who wants to reach their dreams needs a method of determining all the enabling objectives. They will also need a way to receive constant feedback and update their progress.  This app six sees wonderfully in doing just that.

Tech-support has been very responsive. I am a very happy customer.

title: Basic but still missing basics
body:
I like the layout of the app. Clean. Refreshing. It's quick to log. Reminders is nice. But a few key basics it's missing: 1. No way to view each entry or edit each entry. This is inconvenient because you can't tell whether you logged for the day or not nor can you tell what you logged. Also, when I logged my first value I chose add to total but all it did was erase the starting value and put it at the value I had entered. Example: starting value was 200. I logged 4 thinking that would bring my progress to 204 but instead it brought it to 4. I then tried to edit the entry but couldn't find a way to do that. So I decided to log an entry and this time I put my total as 204 but then this time it added it to the 4 it had making it now 208. Ugh. Would appreciate an edit button. 

2. Reminders- a great feature EXCEPT when you already log for the day before the alarm goes off. Because then it keeps that reminder badge thinking that since no input has been made after the reminder was issued that you have not logged anything. I could change the reminder to occur super early but the whole point is to remind at a time when best convenient. And hey, if you remember to log before the reminder you shouldn't be punished with a reminder badge lingering. Also it would be great if I could set multiple reminders for the day. For example I'm trying to get into the habit of logging calories so it would be great if I could have it remind me three times a day. Because with one reminder I may forget the other meals. 

3. Okay the dashboard is nice but without more functionality (like zoom in, see entries, etc) it seems kind of pointless. It would be nice if it would tell you your projected date at current pace and what pace you should have to reach projected date. Perhaps that's too advance but it would be a nice, usable feature. 

Overall, knowing what I know now, would I have paid for it then? Probably not. Maybe $1 but that's it. To me it's missing necessary features for a goal/habit app. It's off to a good start.

title: La mejor app de registro de hábitos que probé.
body:
Es una aplicación excelente.

Pros:
- simplicidad, muy fácil hacer cualquier acción con tus hábitos: crear, registrar, borrar, actualizar
- excelente sync entre iPhone y Mac
- excelente diseño

Contras:
- me tomó un tiempo entender cómo funcionaban algunas cosas, y eso que soy un usuario avanzado, pero era la primera vez que usaba una app de registro de hábitos y eso pudo haber incidido

Probé muchas otras apps de registro de hábitos durante días/semanas: Habitify, Habit Bull, Everyday, Productive, Habitica y TickTick. Strides fue por lejos la mejor app que usé, por eso la elegí y compre el premium. No hubo otra que se le acercara, al menos para mi gusto y necesidades. 
Todas las demás tenían un diseño y experiencia de usuario espantosa o lenta o no eran nada intuitivas. O peor, te ponían el premium en la cara a cada rato para que lo compraras cuando ni siquiera había usado la app por unas horas, suelo descartar automaticamente cualquier producto que haga eso, es nefasto. Algunas te preguntaban que compres el premium APENAS LA DESCARGAS (?!), por favor nunca le hagan eso al usuario, honestamente no se si les funciona pero para personas que somos conscientes de los productos que usamos, suele ser un descarte instantáneo.

Pude intercambiar emails con el Kyle, el CEO, sobre varios temas que quería aclarar antes de comprometerme a usar Strides: exports, longevidad de Strides, funcionalidades sociales, multi plataforma. Sus respuestas fueron rápidas, claras y me dieron la seguridad que Strides era un producto serio.

Compré la suscripción de por vida y vale totalmente la pena, y recomiendo a quien quiera mejorar sus hábitos usar Strides como su herramienta principal, te puede cambiar la vida!

Gracias Strides y Kyle por esta excelente herramienta.
